verdict.rationale: Fellow's own webhooks fire an HTTP POST to a URL you register whenever an event occurs, such as an AI note being generated or an action item completed. That gives event-triggered automation, but any action logic has to live in the user's own endpoint. missing for 10: a user-definable rule engine or conditional trigger configuration, built-in in-product actions executed on events, documentation of event filtering and conditions, independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can define rules that trigger actions automatically on events

citations.quote: When an event happens (like an AI note being generated or an action item being completed), Fellow sends an HTTP POST request to the URL you specify with details about the event.
Webhooks allow you to receive real-time notifications when events occur in Fellow.
This enables you to build integrations that react immediately to changes in Fellow, without needing to poll for updates.
